module.name: orch
module.spec: Init creates an empty .drift/state.xml file by saving an empty State via the caller-provided fileio.Session (see fileio.session). NOT idempotent: if StateStore.Initialized() reports the project is already initialized (state.xml exists on disk), Init returns ErrAlreadyInitialized without writing. If Initialized() returns a non-not-found error (e.g. corrupt state.xml), Init propagates that error rather than overwriting. See cli.init_idempotent for the user-facing contract. See principles.specs_are_truth.

Todo loads State via the caller-provided fileio.Session, scans the filesystem, reconciles specs and markers, builds a CoreAlgorithmContext with TodoAction (propagating baseline Edges), runs the core algorithm to derive closures, and returns the EvaluatedState without saving. The scan's discovered spec-spec Edges are passed via the Scan struct so the core can detect edge add/remove/broken events inside closures. See principles.friction — review without side effects.

ResetClosure receives a caller-provided fileio.Session (see fileio.session) whose lock is already held for the entire Load→modify→Save window. It loads State via the Session, scans the filesystem, reconciles specs and markers, re-derives closures from the current scan+baseline, and locates the closure with the matching 8-character hash. The core applies each event in the closure to baseline: NODE_CHANGED syncs the baseline hash to scan hash; EDGE_ADDED adds the edge to baseline; EDGE_REMOVED removes it; NODE_REMOVED deletes the node and filters its edges; EDGE_BROKEN is a no-op. Closures containing only broken-edge events are refused with ErrResetClosureOnlyBroken. The orchestrator saves the resulting State (Specs, Markers, Edges) via the Session. The saved Edges are exactly the event-synced set the core returned — baseline edges plus only the closure's own EDGE_ADDED/EDGE_REMOVED/NODE_REMOVED effects — so resetting one closure never baselines or drops another closure's pending edge events; newly-cited refs make it into state.xml only when THEIR closure is reviewed and reset. ErrResetClosureNotFound is returned when the hash doesn't match any current closure. See model.provenance closure properties, principles.friction.

Link receives a caller-provided fileio.Session (see fileio.session) whose lock is already held for the entire Load→modify→Save window. It loads State via the Session, scans the filesystem, reconciles, validates that the marker and spec exist, rejects duplicate edges, and saves the State via the Session with a new Edge{From: markerID, To: specID} appended to the EXISTING baseline edges — scanned spec-spec edges are never merged here, so pending EDGE_ADDED/EDGE_REMOVED closures survive a link exactly as they survive an unlink. The write is scoped to the link itself: ONLY a new marker (empty baseline hash) is registered, by copying its scan hash into the reconciled State and writing its content baseline. Link NEVER modifies any spec's baseline hash or content baseline and NEVER absorbs an existing marker's pending drift, so pending NODE_CHANGED/NODE_ADDED closures survive a link exactly as they survive an unlink — a newly linked spec therefore stays pending as NODE_ADDED until it is reviewed and reset. The Session's lock prevents concurrent invocations from silently overwriting each other's edges. See principles.friction.

Unlink receives a caller-provided fileio.Session (see fileio.session) whose lock is already held for the entire Load→modify→Save window. It loads State via the Session, finds the link-style edge matching the given marker and spec, removes it from Edges, and saves the State via the Session. If no matching edge exists, returns an error.

ReconcileSpecs compares baselined specs against scanned specs. Baselined specs not found on disk are kept in the result with Deleted=true and their baseline hash preserved (no error). New specs in the scan get Hash="" (no baseline yet) so that DeriveClosures flags them as NODE_CHANGED on the next todo. Existing specs keep their baselined baseline hash but update filepath and line number. See principles.specs_are_truth.

ReconcileMarkers compares baselined markers against scanned markers. Baselined markers not found on disk are kept in the result with Deleted=true and their baseline hash preserved (no error). New markers in the scan get Hash="" (no baseline yet) so that DeriveClosures flags them as NODE_CHANGED on the next todo. Existing markers keep their baselined baseline hash but update filepath and line number. See principles.specs_are_truth.

DiffClosure loads State, scans, reconciles, re-derives closures, and locates the closure by hash. For each node in the closure, it builds a DiffSide (spec or marker) containing: ID, filepath, line range (markers only), baseline hash, current hash, baseline content (from BaselineStore), current content (read from disk), HasBaseline flag, and Deleted flag. Returns ErrDiffClosureNotFound if the hash doesn't match any current closure. Read-only — does not modify state.

DiffAll returns per-closure diff results alongside the evaluated state. For each closure, it computes DiffSides for every node and returns them as a ClosureDiff struct (Hash, Events, Diffs). Used by `drift diff --all` to render every closure's diffs in one pass.

The orchestrator package declares sentinel error values for every documented failure mode of its public methods: ErrLinkMarkerNotFound, ErrLinkSpecNotFound, ErrLinkAlreadyExists, ErrUnlinkNotFound, ErrDiffClosureNotFound, ErrDiffNodeNotFound, ErrAlreadyInitialized, ErrResetClosureNotFound, and ErrResetClosureOnlyBroken. Each maps a user-facing intent ("I tried to link an unknown marker") to a distinct error so the CLI can pattern-match on errors.Is without parsing strings. The markerSyntax constant ("D! id=<shortcode>") is the canonical hint string surfaced in prescriptive link errors (see cli.prescriptive_link_errors). See core.algorithm_types for the core-side sentinel errors that propagate through EvaluateState (ErrClosureNotFound, ErrBrokenEdgeNotResettable) and are translated by resetClosureInner into the orchestrator-level ErrResetClosureNotFound / ErrResetClosureOnlyBroken.

NewOrchestrator(stateStore, scanner, baselines) wires the four collaborators into an Orchestrator struct: stateStore (the .drift/state.xml persistence layer), scanner (the project-rooted file scanner), core (a fresh CoreAlgorithm constructed internally — never injected, since it is stateless), and baselines (the content-addressed .drift/baselines.bin store, may be nil to disable baseline snapshotting). The Orchestrator is the only place the cli/commands layer touches state-store, scanner, or baseline mutation: every command calls an orchestrator method, never the underlying stores directly. See cli.init_idempotent, orch.todo, orch.reset_closure.

DiffSide, DiffResult, ChangeSummary, NodeChange, and EdgeChange are the diff/summary shape types the orchestrator returns to the CLI for rendering. DiffSide describes one side (spec or marker) of a drift event: ID, Filepath, Lines ("start-end" for markers, "" for specs), BaselineHash, CurrentHash, Baseline content, Current content, HasBaseline flag, and Deleted flag. DiffResult wraps a DiffSide as either Spec or Marker (whichever is non-nil) plus IsSeed (true iff this side's node ID is one of the closure's seeds — see output.diff_seed_label). ChangeSummary{Operation, NodeChanges, EdgeChanges} describes the mutations a state-changing operation applied (or would apply in --dry-run form). NodeChange{ID, Kind "changed"|"added"|"removed", OldHash, NewHash}; EdgeChange{From, To, Kind "added"|"removed"}. Used by ResetClosure, Link, and Unlink in both preview and post-apply forms. See cli.reset_format, cli.link_format, cli.unlink_format, orch.change_summary.

writeBaseline is the internal helper that records a content-addressed baseline snapshot for one spec or marker using its CURRENT scanned hash. It is best-effort: a nil BaselineStore makes it a no-op; any read error from ReadSpecContent / ReadMarkerContent is swallowed (returns nil) so baseline snapshotting failures never fail the caller (the state mutation already succeeded). resolvePath(p) joins the scanner's project root with the relative path stored in state, returning p unchanged if it is already absolute — this bridges the state-stored relative filepath to the absolute path the os file reads require. Called by linkInner after a successful link ONLY when the linked marker is new (records the marker baseline; never the spec's) and by resetClosureInner for every NODE_CHANGED/NODE_ADDED event in the resolved closure. See pinstore.baselines, scanner.spec_content_read, scanner.marker_content_read.

findSpecByID and findMarkerByID are linear-scan lookup helpers that return the matching core.Spec / core.Marker and a bool; false (zero value) when no entry matches. They are used by resetClosureInner to translate a DriftEvent.NodeID back to its full scan-time record (so writeBaseline can read the file at the correct filepath and line range). Linear scan is appropriate because reset touches a handful of events per closure; the alternative (precomputing a map) would dominate the lookup cost for the typical case. See orch.reset_closure, orch.write_baseline_helper.

computeChangeSummary(before, after statestore.State, operation string) ChangeSummary diffs two State values and produces a ChangeSummary enumerating every node and edge mutation. For specs and markers: an ID present in both but with differing Hash yields a NodeChange{Kind:"changed", OldHash, NewHash}; an ID present only in after yields {Kind:"added", NewHash}; an ID present only in before yields {Kind:"removed", OldHash}. For edges: an edge key (From\x00To) present only in after yields EdgeChange{Kind:"added"}; present only in before yields {Kind:"removed"}. The Operation string is caller-supplied ("resolve closure HASH", "link MARKER → SPEC", "unlink MARKER → SPEC") and surfaces in the rendered summary. The function is pure — no I/O, no side effects — and is called by both the preview path (--dry-run, save=false) and the apply path (save=true) of Link/Unlink/ResetClosure so the rendered output matches what was actually written. See output.change_summary_format.

buildScan(scanResult, reconciledSpecs, reconciledMarkers) constructs the core.Scan struct the algorithm consumes. SpecHashes and MarkerHashes start as the scan's hash maps; then any reconciled spec/marker whose ID is NOT in the scan (i.e. a baseline-only deleted entry awaiting NODE_REMOVED reset) gets an empty-string hash entry so DeriveClosures can flag it via the reconciler's sentinel empty-string state. buildScan is the single place where the reconciled-baseline + fresh-scan views are joined into the shape core.EvaluateState expects. See orch.reconcile_specs, orch.reconcile_markers, core.scan_coverage.
